title: How wrf_gpu Works
text: How wrf_gpu Works wrf_gpu is a clean-room JAX rewrite of the WRF-ARW forecast model that targets the GPU memory hierarchy from day one. It reproduces the same physics solver WRF implements, but its architecture, execution model, and validation strategy are built for the GPU — not inherited from the WRF Fortran source. wrf_gpu is not a line-by-line translation of WRF Fortran and it is not a CUDA-annotated copy of the WRF codebase. It is an independent implementation of the WRF-ARW equations and physics, written in JAX and compiled to the GPU through XLA. It reads the same inputs as WRF and writes WRF-compatible output, but the solver in between is its own code, held to WRF's numerical behavior by validation rather than by shared source. Why this matters for you Because it is a rewrite validated against an oracle, wrf_gpu can be honest and precise about exactly which parts match WRF and how well. The sealed identity fixtures prove their dynamics/thermodynamics fields cell-for-cell identical to CPU-WRF v4; this is fixture-backed evidence, not universal control/configuration parity. title: GPU-native architecture
text: The design follows a small set of immutable principles: Whole-state device residency. After initialization the full model state lives on the GPU. There are no host↔device transfers inside the timestep loop (any exception requires an architecture decision record). Fused, timestep-scale kernels. The integrator compiles into a few large fused programs rather than a storm of tiny kernel launches, so the GPU stays busy instead of waiting on launch overhead. WRF's precision. title: Validation against WRF, not bitwise reproducibility
text: wrf_gpu does not aim to be bit-for-bit identical to a specific WRF build (which is impossible across compilers and core counts anyway). Instead it validates against WRF as an oracle through a tiered pyramid, strongest evidence first: Micro-fixture / savepoint parity — individual physics kernels checked against pristine-WRF single-column oracles to machine precision. Physical invariants — conservation and boundedness checks. Short-run / convergence — behavior over the first forecast hours. Cell-identity proof — a full GPU wrfout compared to a CPU-WRF wrfout over all grid cells, all forecast lea

title: The priority order
text: When two goals conflict, wrf_gpu resolves them in a fixed order: stability > identity > speed > memory A result is never destabilized or altered to go faster or fit in less memory. Since v0.3.0 the default path runs the validated fp32 kernels (WRF's own single precision), revalidated against CPU-WRF; other validated fp32 fast paths are release defaults, with explicit opt-outs; performance changes retain their numerical scope. Proven WRF-fidelity fixes may intentionally move results, as v0.23.4 and v0.3.0 do; affected trajectories must then be revalidated. See Performance & GPU Modes.

title: Installation & Requirements
text: Installation & Requirements wrf_gpu is a JAX/CUDA application: an Ampere-or-newer NVIDIA GPU (compute capability ≥8.0), a CUDA 13 JAX build, and Python. title: Quickstart: Your First Forecast
text: Quickstart: Your First Forecast Run the bundled Switzerland 3 km case — real GFS-initialized inputs that ship in the repo — end-to-end on your GPU in three commands, then read the WRF-compatible wrfout it writes. No external data download, no local real.exe step, no CPU-WRF run required. Before you start You need wrf_gpu installed with a GPU-visible JAX (Installation & Requirements). The bundled case selects RRTMG radiation and Noah-MP land; Noah-MP reads WRF lookup tables, so set GPUWRF_WRF_ROOT to a pristine WRF v4 tree first. This case needs only GPUWRF_WRF_ROOT — GPUWRF_CANAIRY_ROOT is for the larger validation corpus, not this case. # 1. Point at a pristine WRF v4 source/run tree (for the RRTMG + Noah-MP tables): export GPUWRF_WRF_ROOT=/path/to/WRF # 2. Run one forecast hour of the bundled Switzerland 3 km case on the GPU: python -m gpuwrf.cli run \ --input-dir examples/switzerland_d01 \ --output-dir runs/switzerland_d01 \ --domain d01 \ --hours 1 \ --scratch-dir /fast/nvme/scratch # any real (non-tmpfs) fast disk # 3. Read the WRF-compatible history file: ncdump -h runs/switzerland_d01/wrfout_d01_* Raise --hours for a longer forecast — the bundled namelist window covers 24 h.

title: Input Data & Initialization
text: Input Data & Initialization wrf_gpu keeps the WRF run artifacts you already know: namelist.input, wrfinput_*, and wrfbdy_d01. It integrates those real-data inputs on the GPU with no CPU-WRF wrfout dependency, and auto-detects a legacy replay path when CPU-WRF wrfout history is present. Usage parity with WRF If you already run WRF, the biggest change is that wrf_gpu replaces wrf.exe with a single command, python -m gpuwrf.cli run. You keep your WRF real-data case directory and namelist.input; the supported namelist matrix runs as-is, and anything unsupported fails closed with a named reason. Operational The primary path is standalone native-init. The current CLI reads the model's initial state from wrfinput_<domain> and the root lateral-boundary forcing from wrfbdy_d01. There is no CPU-WRF wrfout replay in the loop; the forecast state is advanced by wrf_gpu on the GPU. A standalone case directory looks like a normal WRF real-data case: my_case/ ├── namelist.input # standard WRF v4 ARW namelist (bring your own) ├── wrfinput_d01 # initial state (one per domain you run) ├── wrfinput_d02 ├── wrfbdy_d01 # lateral boundaries for the outer domain └── met_em.d0*.*.nc # met_em-stage forcing

title: Dynamical Core
text: Dynamical Core wrf_gpu integrates a nonhydrostatic, split-explicit ARW dynamical core on the GPU — the same architecture as WRF's Advanced Research WRF core, re-implemented in JAX and validated cell-for-cell against CPU-WRF as the oracle. Sealed identity fixtures prove their dynamics/thermodynamics fields cell-for-cell identical to CPU-WRF v4; this is not a universal control/configuration claim, and the path-specific gaps below remain open. The priority order is stability > identity > speed > memory, with no masking, clamping, or nan_to_num on the result path. The core uses WRF's split-explicit time scheme. A third-order Runge-Kutta (RK3) large step advances the slow (meteorologically significant) modes, while the fast acoustic and gravity-wave modes are integrated with smaller acoustic sub-steps inside each RK3 stage. Only rk_order=3 is supported. Native single-root and live-nested runs honor time_step_sound. Zero or omission derives WRF automatic sound steps from dt/grid spacing (4 on the tracked grid). The legacy CPU-history replay driver has a separate historical default of 10; it is not the native default. Both native and compatibility replay builders bind requested moist_adv_

title: Nesting
text: Nesting wrf_gpu runs one-way live nesting — validated on the three-domain Tenerife release gate in v0.3.0 and through d01 → … → d09 on the v0.23.4 one-hour fixture — entirely on the GPU. The parent domain advances and builds each child's lateral boundary live during the run, so you do not need a pre-supplied wrfbdy_d02. The child's initial condition comes from its own wrfinput_d0N; only wrfbdy_d01 forces the root. There is no CPU-WRF wrfout dependency. The nested driver is a standalone recursion faithful to WRF's module_integrate sub-cycling: the parent advances one step, constructs each child's lateral-boundary package from its own freshly-advanced state, and recurses into the child, which sub-cycles to catch up to the parent's clock. Each child's boundary update cadence is its parent's timestep. This is the validated one-way wiring (parent → child; the child does not modify the parent). The nest refinement is set by the WRF &domains key parent_grid_ratio (the spatial refinement, e.g. 3), read from the domain metadata. title: The first run compiles
text: A new source, geometry or target can spend minutes compiling before integration. Cold setup is a separate cost from a warm forecast. Run a new geometry/version alone once before attempting concurrent cold builds. No quiet-host W3 compile or warm-readiness number is inferred from the old benchmark.

title: Reuse compatible executables
text: Later compatible runs reuse caches. Native nested AOT prefetch defaults ON; OFF loads at first dispatch. Compatibility includes target and effective controls. A copied cache can safely refuse a fingerprint mismatch even when pin-file contents match: path-bearing XLA flags are part of the target binding. Refusal is not a forecast failure or permission to bypass compatibility checks.

The all-four-running steady window measured 4.857 s/case-hour, 25.4×. Whole-run clocks include init/load and output, without compression. The FIFO tail is not the steady-window throughput number. A reserved pool needs outside-pool headroom; an unreserved pool also needs its budget. Explicit allocator settings win. Cold compilation and warm forecasts have different host peaks.
